405 Biltmore Way, Coral Gables,  FL

City Commission Mayor Vince Lago Vice Mayor Rhonda Anderson Commissioner Melissa Castro Commissioner Ariel Fernandez Commissioner Kirk Menendez

City Manager,  Amos Rojas,  Jr. City Attorney,  Cristina SuÆrez

Agenda Item F-10 [ 4:40 p.m.] Update on the P-Card audit.

Sponsored by Commissioner Fernandez)

Mayor Lago:   Moving on to F-10.  Commissioner Fernandez.

Commissioner Fernandez:   I think staff had a presentation.

Finance Director Gomez: Good afternoon. Diana Gomez,  Finance Director. For the record, Celeste Walker- Harmon had to leave for a medical appointment,  but she is on the Zoom.   So, if we have questions for Celeste,  she' s available on the Zoom,  I was told.   So at the January 23rd,

City Commission Meeting

April 16, 2024

Agenda Item F-10 - Update

on the P-Card audit.

2023 Commission meeting,  the City Commission directed that an audit be initiated to review the Amazon P-Card purchases for the City to determine if any misuse or violations of the program existed.   This item is to provide an update as to the status of that audit.   We' ve already provided the Commission via email,  a preliminary report for the eight- month period from June 2023 to January 2024, as information was readily available in our new financial management system.   We are actively working on the remaining 16 months of information;  however,  that has proven to be much more of a manually intensive process and will take a little bit longer than the three months that we originally discussed at that first meeting.   So, we expect that that portion of the review to be completed in the next six to eight weeks.   So, one,  we wanted to inform you that we were not ready within the three months that we originally asked for.  We need a little bit of extra time.  So, the Amazon transactions made by departmental users are reviewed by department directors and then by the Procurement Division of the Finance Department each month with a P-Card reconciliation process.   Procurement- specific duties are to enforce and monitor the guidelines in place for the program, while the department directors have the discretion and ultimate responsibility for determining and approving what purchases are necessary for them to conduct business and to maintain operations for the respective departments. When we performed their subsequent review of the Amazon transactions,  we found that there was no misuse of City funds had been identified. All purchases were made in accordance with City and departmental past practices and policies in effect at the time.  So, I don' t know if there' s any specific questions,  but that' s so far what we have found with the eight- month period that we have looked at.

Commissioner Fernandez: Right,  so I guess,  as I mentioned earlier,  I understand that based on past practices,  you did not find anything that' s inappropriate.   And having conversations with the Manager,  new procedures have been put in place and new protocols to ensure that there are no questionable charges in these reports going forward.   But I don' t agree with the fact that taxpayer dollars were not spent in a way that they shouldn' t have.   Buying gifts for --  wedding gifts for people,  you know, $ 12,000 in Amazon gift cards. I understand they were for employees at an event,  but for the --

Finance Director Gomez:   Yeah, those were reimbursed by the insurance companies.

Commissioner Fernandez:   Right.

Finance Director Gomez:   So taxpayer dollars did not pay for that.

Commissioner Fernandez:   But at the end of the day, it is, because that' s --  we paid that insurance company,  we got that as a credit for training that staff was doing.   There has to be a better way to do it.  I understand that having reviewed this,  you have said there' s nothing wrong.   In some of these charges,  I don' t know who approved it.   In this report,  some of them,  the name of the individual is, and some of the most questionable ones,  the former City Manager was blamed for the approval.   There' s other things that,  you know, I brought up the steamer as one of the things last time. And the response here is that the steamer was being used to -for tablecloths in

Development Services. Well,  it just so happens I went to one of those lunches at development services.   There was no tablecloth.   So,  where' s the tablecloth?   And as far as my conversations with folks there,  there are no tablecloths in Development Services. So,  I understand we have a reason for everything and your team has done a great job of putting this together,  but I'm not comfortable with the results.  And that' s why when the Mayor brings up doing a full forensic audit, I think that that may be the direction we have to go.  I'm not comfortable with these results.   And I understand,  you know, it took a lot of time to do this.   And what you have told me is it's going to take a lot more time to do the prior year and four months because it is a different software and there is more paper trail that has to be tracked down.   But honestly in seeing this, I think we have to.   We need to continue to look into this.   And as I've mentioned before,  this is just Amazon. There' s tons of other things that have been paid for with our P-Cards which I'm now asking questions about because Amazon is an easy one to track.  The information is there online, you can print out a list of everything that you' ve purchased with the dates,  what was paid.   So, you know, I appreciate the work that has put in, but even though I had preliminarily told you let' s focus on one department,  I think we need to continue the audit the way that it was being done.

Finance Director Gomez:   And we have been.

Commissioner Fernandez:   And as long as it takes to get the final results.   And I appreciate the fact that the Manager has taken lead on this and changing some of these protocols because some things were basically falling through the cracks because there was no set protocol on what could and could not be done.   I spent 13 years working in Congress.   You basically had --  when you were putting in for a specific charge,  you almost had to give blood to prove that it was actually a charge that you should be putting in.  But there was definitely no, you know,  congressionally provided, you know, supplies for us to cook in a kitchen.   I'm wondering why we even have a cooktop in Development Services.   That' s a fire hazard.   It' s not a place that' s equipped to do this kind of -to have somebody cooking.   Headphones,  we had to bring them from home.   You know, when we were giving a gift to somebody who was --  and I'm not talking to you directly.   You' re here --

Finance Director Gomez:   Sure.

Commissioner Fernandez:  -because you' ve done the audit.   I think it' s in general.   We need to be more conscious about the money that we' re spending.   And like the Mayor received calls from employees that this is a morale issue,  I've received calls from employees who believe that this is a positive morale booster because there' s more accountability and there' s going to be a process in place that makes it easier for them to make decisions when they' re putting in for a charge.   So,  I appreciate all the work that' s been done,  but I think we need to continue moving forward.   And I applaud you, Mr. Manager,  for putting in some fixes to some of the issues that we' ve been having. I know coffee was one of the things that was brought up and you have completely changed the policy on coffee moving forward.  And I think we' re taking the right steps to fix what, as I brought when I brought this up, I said we wanted to make sure there was no public corruption.   And I think it would be a big positive for the City if we find no public corruption in this.  That would be

great. But there are questionable charges. Even if we want to say there aren' t questionable charges,  there are questionable charges. Mayor Lago:   But if I may.

Finance Director Gomez:   I think it's a judgment call.

Mayor Lago:   If I may --  but if I may.
